To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated that semisynthetic ZnChls can be organized in 2D stacked and 1D tubular assemblies, which exhibit efficient charge transport with room temperature mobilities as high 0.28 and 0.07 (cm(2) V)(-1) s(-), respectively.
we have observed efficient charge mobility in self-assembled semisynthetic porphyrinoid materials, which opens the way for supramolecular electronic devices based on natural systems.
semisynthetic chlorin dyes can form either 2D brickwork or 1D tubular assemblies in the solid state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new synthetic routes for the preparation of semisynthesized chlorin derivatives and the study of their charge transport properties.
the development of new materials for organic electronic devices, based on the self-assembly of semisynthesized zinc chlorin porphyrins (ZnClps).
the synthesis of new semisynthetic chlorin derivatives, their supramolecular self-assembly in the solid state and the study of their electronic properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have observed efficient charge transporting capabilities in semisynthesized chlorin assemblies.

the charge transport in these semisynthetic ZnChls is very efficient, and the mobility is comparable to that of the best organic semiconductors, such as poly(3-hexylthiophene), and the best conjugated polymers.
the supramolecular assembly is the key factor for efficient charge transport, while the molecular structure of the individual ZnChl plays a secondary role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that semisynthetic chlorins can form highly organized assemblies with charge transport properties that are superior to those observed for natural chlorins.
the semisynthetic Zn chlorins are excellent building blocks for molecular wires and that their charge transport properties can be tuned by changing their molecular structures.

semisynthetic chlorophyll derivatives can be used as molecular building blocks for supramolecular electronic devices, which can be used as a platform for the development of new materials for solar energy conversion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supramolecular organization of the ZnChl molecules is crucial for the charge transporting properties of these materials.
it shows how supramolecular assemblies can be used to control the charge transport properties in semisynthesized systems.
the charge transport properties are strongly dependent on the molecular structure of the chlorins, the organization of the molecules in the assemblies, and the solvent.
